## TL;DR

Release emails work for any project that has `[auth.emailProvider]` set up. When `[release.email]` is on, a stable cut sends each recipient one email with the version, the notes, the known issues typed in the release modal, and links. By default it waits until GitHub serves the release with its assets. This pass fixed the defects review pass 1 found: a restart could leave a send stuck `pending` with no way to resend, send failures were silent, the bell notice was missing, and Resend had no timeout. The scoped `repoos check` result is recorded in the handoff, not here. Still open: the "send test email" action, a CLI subcommand, and a visual check of the card in its sent and pending states.

## Work and rationale

**Restart recovery.** A `pending` record with no waiter in this process cannot finish, so `getReleaseEmailRecord` now reads it as `failed` with a restart reason. The Resend button then appears. I did not rewrite the file on read, because the read path should not write. The first version of this fix checked the on-disk status only; the in-process `inFlight` set is what separates a live wait from an orphan, so a live send keeps showing "Waiting for GitHub".

**Silent failures.** The detached start (`startCutReleaseEmail`) used to swallow every error. The record read now sits inside the `try`, so a corrupt `release-emails.json` lands in the existing failure path. If even the record write fails, the start logs and raises the bell item. The Releases page load also used to hide errors behind an empty `catch`. It now shows the message and clears it on the next successful load.

**Bell notice.** Acceptance item 3 asked for one. A `releaseEmailFailed` attention kind now exists, with `warning` severity and a link to `/releases`. `recordFor` raises it for a `failed` record, or a `skipped` record when no provider is configured. A `sent` record clears it. The id is one per version, so a retry replaces the notice rather than stacking it. The kind is added to `AttentionKind`, the recorded-event union and the durable-event validator (`src/server/attention-events.ts`), without which a stored notice would be dropped on reload.

**Timeouts.** `sendEmail` now passes an `AbortSignal.timeout(15s)`, which also bounds reading the error body. Before this, a hung Resend call kept the record `pending` and the in-flight slot taken until restart. The publish probe already had a 10-second timeout.

**Publish detection.** Review pointed out that a 403 or 429 on the first look triggered the tag fallback, which defeats the `published` default under GitHub's unauthenticated rate limit. Now only a request that gets no answer counts as "no network". An HTTP error keeps waiting until the one-hour timeout. I documented the private-repository case (the public API returns 404, so the email waits and then fails) and pointed those users to `when = "tagged"`.

**Tests.** I added 9 tests to `src/ui-app/tests/release-email.test.ts`, which pass along with the rest of the suite (50 in that file). They cover the orphaned-pending read and Resend recovery, the HTTP-error wait, the abort signal, the bell raised and cleared, the missing-provider bell, the corrupt-log detached start, the Resend route's refusal and version check, the preview 404, and both rejection paths of the Settings recipient branch. The route tests pass a `Buffer` body. A `Readable` of plain strings reads as an empty body, which made the first run fail with misleading 400s.

**Shots.** I declared two shots on the task: the Releases email card (highlighting `[data-test-id="release-email"]`) and the Settings section. No state fixture exists for a sent or pending email, so the capture shows whatever the preview board renders. I did not confirm the highlight against the live page, because RepoOS captures shots at handoff.

## Approaches tried

- **Fix restart recovery on read versus on startup.** I could have rewritten orphaned records when the server boots. A read-side fix needs no boot hook and cannot race a live send, so I chose it.
- **Bell via the existing attention-events store.** The store is a per-process object; a second instance would overwrite the file with stale data. I routed through the `attention-notify` helpers, which the server already wires up.
- **Publish fallback on every error versus only network errors.** Treating every error as "unavailable" was simpler, but it made the default `published` behaviour unreliable under rate limits. The narrower rule adds one enum variant.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Test bodies.** The first route tests failed with 400s. The cause was the test double, not the handlers: `readBody` concatenates `Buffer` chunks, and my `Readable` yielded strings.
- **Shots need a human-visible check.** I can declare the shots, but the captured PNGs only exist after handoff. I have not opened them, so the visual acceptance criterion is not verified yet.
- **Acceptance 2 wording.** The spec asks for a "send test email" action as well as the preview. I built the preview, which renders without sending. A send-to-self test needs a decision about who receives it, so I left it out and recorded it as a gap.

## Key learnings

- `Readable.from` on strings is not a request body for code that concatenates `Buffer`s. Use `Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(...))` in route tests.
- A file-backed "pending" state is only trustworthy together with an in-process owner. Without the owner check, a restart leaves a record that looks live forever.
- A failure that is caught and dropped is worse than one that is noisy. Every path that can fail after the release is out now either records the failure or logs it, and most do both.
